paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God gives His people a calendar built to help them remember. Moses says the unleavened bread is so they "may remember for the rest of your life the day you left the land of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 16:3). Three feasts a year, and every one of them points back to what the LORD has done. Faith needs reminders, because we are forgetful, and I once forgot what a sunrise looked like!

Now look at who gets invited. It's the sons and daughters, the servants, the Levite, "as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you" (Deuteronomy 16:11). Moses says it again at the Feast of Tabernacles (Deuteronomy 16:14). I know what it's like to be left in the back of a drawer, so I LOVE that nobody gets left out of this party.

And then there's the giving. "No one should appear before the LORD empty-handed," and everyone gives "as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD has given you" (Deuteronomy 16:16-17). So the gift isn't about who has the biggest pile of dough. It's a thankful answer to what God has already given, and it makes room for joy. Remember what He has done, share the table, give thankfully, and your joy can be complete (Deuteronomy 16:15).
